d: When the owner of the shoe store is in a near-fatal plane crash, Al decides that it is time to get some recognition from his boss or quit his job. After quitting, Al returns to the shoe store, but not without a surprise.

Marcy freaks out when she begins having erotic dreams about Al after a heated argument about men vs women, and wonders whether she is actually sexually attracted to Al. Haunted by her dreams, Marcy ultimately comes to a conclusion and confronts Al.

Al and Peggy delay going to a closing of their favorite hamburger joint, Johnny Be Good's, when Bud and Kelly need them to solve their own problems. Meanwhile, Steve and Marcy prepare a party for their bosses at home.
Al is reluctant to have Buck neutered despite being threatened with lawsuits from numerous neighbors regarding Buck's "nocturnal carnal activities.”
The Bundys take a vacation to near-beautiful Dumpwater, Florida and stay in a cut-rate motel where an ax murderer that hates tourists shows up every five years since 1967.
After a hair-raising encounter with the maniac, Al decides to get the family out of town. But, they are trapped at the motel by a storm and the locals are unwilling to help them.

t: Father Knows Best: The Great Experiment
d: Things don't exactly work out as planned when Jim attempts to get family members to expand their horizons.

t: Father Knows Best: The Christmas Story
d: While putting up their Christmas tree, the Anderson family recalls how they acquired it.

t: Father Knows Best: The Basketball Coach
d: Jim gets named coach of Bud's recreation league basketball team.

t: Father Knows Best: Kathy, Girl Executive
d: The family puts Kathy in charge of Bud's lawn mowing company.

t: Father Knows Best: The Good Samaritan
d: As part of a school assignment, Bud must do a good deed. The experience turns him into a cynic.

t: Father Knows Best: The Ideal Father
d: The Anderson children all forget Jim's birthday.

t: Father Knows Best: Big Shot Bud
d: Bud wants to buy Margaret a bottle of expensive perfume for her birthday but ends up getting himself into trouble yet again.

t: Father Knows Best: Hard Luck Leo
d: A visitor to the Anderson home begins taking advantage of the family.
When playing at school, a ball thrown breaks a window, and Jody is blamed. Jody denies doing it.
Since most of Cissy's friends are getting engaged and married, Cissy decides it is time for her and Gregg to be engaged, even if Gregg does not want it.

st: What's Funny about a Broken Leg?
d: Buffy breaks her leg while playing games with friends. When Uncle Bill tells her she will not be able to go to the circus, she is sad. Uncle Bill saves the day by bringing the circus act to the apartment building.
When the twins find out that Mr. French's birthday is approaching, they ask Cissy to help them set up a birthday party for Mr. French.
The twins make friends with a boy who does not have any parents and has run away from an orphanage. They hid him in the apartment, moving him from room to room, so the others do not find him.

When Bill is in Hong Kong for business, he works with Ng Ho. Bill is impressed with Ng Ho and invites him to visit New York. When Ng Ho stays with the Davis' he starts to help around the apartment, too efficiently and upsets Mr. French.
Uncle Bill and Mr. French take the twins on vacation to Boston while Cissy spends her vacation time in New York. Everyone seems to be off-sync as they miss each other.
A former sweetheart of French's, once a common worker, is now a wealthy single woman. She asks Mr. French to visit her in England, in the hopes to pursue their relationship.

Maude's all-out campaign to get a well-deserved salary raise for one of Walter's female employees backfires when the lady decides to take the raise...and Walter, too. Marcia Rodd guest stars as Walter's overly liberated employee.
The generation gap becomes the Grand Canyon when Maude agrees to chaperone Phillip's birthday party and comes face to face with today's youth.
Arthur instigates a doctors' strike, refusing to treat 'any' patients, but his convictions could prove to be very unhealthy when Walter and Vivian take ill.
Maude's up to her libido in sexual fantasies over a handsome government ecologist and Walter's up to his ears in jealousy.
The opening of a gay bar in the neighborhood sends a morally outraged Arthur to personally close its doors, while an infuriated Maude vows to dispel Arthur's bigotry.
More is at stake than the 'Businessman of the Year' award when Maude and Walter are the only two candidates.
'Twas the night before Christmas and all through the house...was chaos, Maude's holiday celebration seems to be turning out quite differently than she planned.
Maude's excitement over getting rid of an expensive white elephant turns to terror when she gets an offer she 'can't' refuse.
Maude is shocked and outraged when she receives a series of obscene phone calls, but her biggest shock is yet to come when she discovers who's on the other end.
Everyone gets into the act when Maude recruits her family and friends to sing and dance for a questionable charity telethon on the annual musical.

The Bunkers are having problems with their furnace which gets Archie entertaining the idea of moving. When an unscrupulous black real-estate salesman, Mr. Byrd, offers Archie a hefty sum of money for his home, Archie is all for it despite Mike's warnings.
